  -- Since Z is zero, it is projective (as all zero objects are projective)
  let hZ_proj : CategoryTheory.Projective Z := infer_instance
  -- The morphism p : I ⟶ Z is not necessarily epi, but since I is injective and Z is zero,
  -- we can use the contrapositive or dual of known lemmas.
  -- Instead, we use the fact that injective objects have the lifting property with respect to monomorphisms
  -- into zero objects. This follows from the duality between injective and projective objects.
  -- We use the lemma that if I is injective and Z is zero, then any morphism i : A ⟶ B with Mono i
  -- has the lifting property with respect to p : I ⟶ Z.
  -- This is a standard result in category theory, which we now formalize using existing lemmas.
  -- We apply the lemma `Projective.hasLiftingProperty_of_isZero` via its dual.
  -- Note: Since I is injective, it is projective in the opposite category.
  -- Therefore, we consider the op category and apply the lemma there.
  let hI_proj : CategoryTheory.Projective I := infer_instance
  let h_op : CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty p.op i.op :=
    CategoryTheory.Projective.hasLiftingProperty_of_isZero p.op i.op hI_proj (by exact CategoryTheory.Epi.of_mono (by exact CategoryTheory.Mono.of_mono i)) hZ
  exact CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_op i p h_op
